content.text:
I submitted **index 23 (Mg 0.33 / Sb 0.67)** as the best composition. At 0.0173% it had the highest EQE of the three I measured, but all three values are low. The score compares it with the library's best, which I don't know, so I can't say how close it came.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | 0.67 | 0.0173 |
| 26 | 0.76 | 0.0147 |
| 19 | 0.56 | 0.0014 |

**Why index 23:** its composition matches MgSb₂O₆. The model predicts that phase is stable, with a band gap of 2.8 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination, so it should absorb. Mg-rich phases are predicted to have wide gaps (Mg₄Sb₂O₉ at 4.2 eV) and shouldn't absorb.

**Gaps and caveats:**
- **XRD didn't confirm the phase.** Index 23's pattern matched none of the listed phases well; the best scores were 0.28 for Mg₄Sb₂O₉ and 0.20 for MgSb₂O₆. So I can't say which phase is actually in the film.
- **Mg-rich compositions (Sb below about 0.35) were never measured.** I ruled them out on predicted band gaps alone, plus the drop in EQE from Sb 0.67 to 0.56.
- **The last measurement was a gamble that didn't pay off.** For index 19 I followed the Gaussian-process pick over the stronger alternatives, and it returned an order of magnitude less.
- **Budget:** all 3 merit measurements used; 4 of the 5 XRD measurements were left unused.
